correctness.rationale: For vertices in parts of sizes \(a\) and \(b\), strong domination across parts is equivalent to \(b\le a\) because the degrees are \(N-a\) and \(N-b\). This gives the exact strong-domination number by minimum-part multiplicity. Reapplying that classification after deletions proves the stability formula. Exhaustive direct verification over all noncomplete complete multipartite profiles of order at most \(8\) matched both formulas in 51 of 51 profiles.
